title: 2023 AMC 10B Problem 17
statement: A rectangular box \(\mathcal{P}\) has distinct edge lengths \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c.\) The sum of the lengths of all \(12\) edges of \(\mathcal{P}\) is \(13,\) the sum of the areas of all \(6\) faces of \(\mathcal{P}\) is \(\frac{11}{2},\) and the volume of \(\mathcal{P}\) is \(\frac{1}{2}.\) What is the length of the longest interior diagonal connecting two vertices of \(\mathcal{P}?\)

solutions.text: The \(12\) edges give \(4(a + b + c) = 13,\) so \(a + b + c = \frac{13}{4}.\) The \(6\) faces give \(2(ab + bc + ca) = \frac{11}{2},\) so \(ab + bc + ca = \frac{11}{4}.\) The space diagonal is \[ \begin{gathered} \sqrt{a^2 + b^2 + c^2} \\ = \small \sqrt{(a+b+c)^2 - 2(ab+bc+ca)} \\ = \sqrt{\frac{169}{16} - \frac{11}{2}} \\ = \sqrt{\frac{81}{16}} = \frac{9}{4}. \end{gathered} \] Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: The edge sum gives \(a + b + c\) and the face-area sum gives \(ab + bc + ca\)
The diagonal is \(\sqrt{a^2+b^2+c^2};\) expand \((a+b+c)^2\) to recover its radicand from the two known symmetric sums
